name: Senkawa
tagline: Shinjuku in 17 minutes and Shibuya in 22 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Toshima City, where Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 27 minutes to Otemachi, 17 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 43 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 32.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.0 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 32.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 32.5 m to 35.5 m, a difference of 3.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 2 clinics and 4 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 敬愛病院, about 18 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 練馬総合病院, about 20 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line also call here. Both lines are run by Tokyo Metro, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line runs at 117%. Its busiest stretch is 要町→池袋, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kanamecho is ahead on the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Senkawa in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 3 minutes sooner than Senkawa. One-room rents run about ¥6,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: Higashi-Nagasaki is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Senkawa is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Senkawa in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Senkawa.

leads.groceries: There are 3 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
